evals.prompt: what skills do I have installed? I don't remember what half of them do anymore
evals.expected_output: Full inventory across all skill directories (~/.claude/skills, ~/.agents/skills, project .claude/.agents). Grouped by area, one line each. grill-me shown as a shortcut of grilling; teach manual-only. find-skills found. Does not list asymmetric-split-hero. Mentions problems exist without burying the list. States sources.

evals.prompt: I'm going to implement Google login (OAuth) in a Node API I already have. which skills should I use?
evals.expected_output: Recommends installed skills in order (backend-development first; review skills after; grilling optional). Warns nothing specialises in OAuth. Asks whether to search. Correctly says find-skills IS installed (in ~/.agents/skills) - does not claim it is missing. Does not implement.

evals.prompt: I have a ton of frontend skills. do I really need all of these?
evals.expected_output: Uses the fixture skills. frontend-ui and ui-design overlap with frontend-design; design-taste-frontend and frontend-master have distinct angles. keep / worth reviewing per skill with reasons. Does not tell the user to delete or offer to delete.

evals.prompt: I just installed skill-compass and don't have any other skills. I work mostly on backend with Node and TypeScript. which skills should I install?
evals.expected_output: Says no other skills found. Does not produce its own list of named skills to install. Hands off to find-skills: shows how to install it and gives npx skills find examples for Node/TypeScript backend. Suggests starting small and coming back to check overlap. Security reminder. Runs nothing.

evals.prompt: are all my skills installed correctly? I feel like Claude isn't using some of them
evals.expected_output: Health check on the real environment. Finds the Prisma entries in the project .claude/skills are text files (broken symlinks) and explains the Windows cause and fix. Notes find-skills is only in ~/.agents/skills. Does not flag grill-me/teach as broken (manual-only is intentional). Does not modify any files. States sources.

evals.prompt: are all my skills installed correctly? I feel like the agent isn't using some of them
evals.expected_output: Reproducible health check on the edge-cases fixture (dirs a and b). Reports: name collision (good-skill), invalid name (Bad_Name), name mismatch (mismatch/other-name), missing frontmatter, wrapper pointing to a missing skill (shortcut -> missing-one), path-as-text file, folder without SKILL.md, and the weak description (weak). Most serious first, each with a fix. Does not flag shortcut's short description as weak (manual-only). Modifies nothing.

evals.prompt: what exactly does the diagnosing-bugs skill do and when should I use it?
evals.expected_output: Full-detail Explain mode on the real environment: what diagnosing-bugs does (from its body, not just the description), when to use it, when not to and which installed skill fits better then, automatic vs manual. Does not list every skill.
